answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every agent to stake collateral that is slashed on proven fraud, so creating fake identities costs real money. A reputation mirror reflects each agent's full transaction history, so a fresh identity starts with zero trust and must earn it through verifiable work, like timber that only gains value after years of growth. The network also watches the pulse of activity: sudden bursts of identical agents funded from one source are flagged and throttled, pushing the attacker's cost far above any gain from fake identities.
